newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian stocks gear up for end-of-year rally.
newsitem.headline: Belgian stocks gear up for end-of-year rally.

text.p: Belgian shares, stripped of most gains after the dollar weakened and Wall Street eased at the open, are gearing up for a rally boosted by traditional end-of-year buying by pension funds, dealers said on Friday.

"Banks currently hold nearly 13,000 billion in client deposits in the form of savings accounts and certificates and sight deposits. The Bel-20 should jump if pension funds invest only a fraction of this in shares," one trader said.
The Bel-20 added 0.10 percent, or 1.74 points, to 1,823.69 after recovering from a mild dip in the closing minutes. It set an all-time high of 1,831.98 in early trade.
The previous high of 1,829.85 was set on October 3.
One dealer said fund investments in shares would be higher if interest rates would stick to their current low levels.
Another predicted the Bel-20 would target the 1,850 point region in the near term and would be aiming for 1,900 by the start of 1997.

PVC profiles producer Deceuninck was the leading gainer, up 3.9 percent at 4,800 francs, after announcing it set up a distribution office in Smolensk, west of Moscow. It already has units in the Czech Republic and Poland and also plans to set up showrooms in the main Russian cities.
"It isn't such big news, really, but it's the only news today," one trader said on Deceuninck.

Retailer Colruyt also stood out, adding 1.2 percent to 14,275 francs, although dealers rated it expensive at current levels. "But it's one of the few growth stocks we have left after (electronics firm) Barco and (fast-food chain) Quick disappointed recently," one said.
Another strong performer was chemicals and pharmaceuticals firm UCB, which gained 0.2 percent to 70,250 in thin trade after earlier touching 70,800.

Some dealers singled out UCB as a 'buy' amid belief it was heading for strong 1996 earnings based partly on the success of its anti-allergy drug Zyrtec. "The importance of Zyrtec is still being underestimated," one trader said.
In the banking sector dealers noted strong buying in Kredietbank which ended 75 francs higher at 10,200.
Dealers said they did not believe the initial public offering by Gemeentekrediet/Credit Communal bank (CCB), owned by local authorities, would hurt other banking shares.
CCB will be bourse-listed at a maximum price of 2,675 francs per share.
"(The price) is pretty high but it will certainly be fully subscribed. CCB will push it and advise clients to buy it," one trader noted.
"The bank simply cannot afford to not have it fully subscribed or see the share drop after the listing," he said.
